blocks.text: In all aqueous solutions the concentrations of H+ and OH- are too low to be conveniently expressed and used in calculations. In 1909 Sorenson, a Danish biochemist, introduced the terms pH and pOH, and the pH and pOH scales were developed: pH = -log[H+] and pOH = -log[OH-]. For neutral water pH = -log(10^-7) = 7 and pOH = 7, and pH + pOH = 14. The value of pH normally varies between 0 and 14 at 25 degrees C, although solutions of negative pH and of pH above 14 are also known. Figure 9.1 lists the pH values of some familiar aqueous solutions, which helps in judging the acidic or basic nature of common solutions.

blocks.alt: Double-headed arrow shaded red (acidic) to white (neutral) to blue (basic); pH 0 to 14 below, [H3O+] 10^0 to 10^-14 above, Neutral at 10^-7. Inside: HCl (1.0 M) pH 0.0, stomach acid pH 1.0-3.0, lemon juice pH 2.2-2.4, vinegar pH 2.4-3.4, carbonated water pH 3.9, beer pH 4.0-4.5, milk pH 6.4, blood pH 7.4, seawater pH 7.0-8.3, baking soda (0.1 M) pH 8.4, milk of magnesia pH 10.5, household ammonia pH 11.9, NaOH (1.0 M) pH 14.0.

blocks.text: Sample Problem 9.1: Kw from a pH of 9.2

The pH of a solution is 9.2; determine Kw at 25 degrees C. First the pOH: pOH = 14 - pH = 14 - 9.2 = 4.8. Then the concentrations by taking antilogs: [OH-] = 10^-pH, [H+] = 10^-9.2, [OH-] about 6.3 x 10^-10 M, and [OH-] = 10^-pOH = 10^-4.8, about 1.6 x 10^-5 M.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The pH gives the H+ concentration, not OH-: [H+] = 10^-pH = 10^-9.2 = 6.3 x 10^-10 M. The OH- concentration comes from the pOH: [OH-] = 10^-4.8 = 1.6 x 10^-5 M.
Sample Problem 9.2: [OH-], pH and pOH from Kw

Kw = 1.0 x 10^-14 at 25 degrees C and the concentration of H+ ions in a solution is 1.0 x 10^-7 M. From Kw = [H+][OH-], 1.0 x 10^-14 = (1.0 x 10^-7)[OH-], so [OH-] = 1.0 x 10^-14 / 1.0 x 10^-7 = 1.0 x 10^-14. Then pH = -log(1.0 x 10^-7) = 7 and pOH = -log(1.0 x 10^-7) = 7.
A copper-etching solution is 0.30 M HNO3. Find [H+], pH, [OH-] and pOH at 25 degrees C.
